blocks.text: This article provides a summary of all new features and enhancements for Secure Access to AI Apps.
The Audit Log page in AI Guard has received the following upgrades:

blocks.item: In the Initiator column, you will now see the username and email listed instead of just the email address.
The initiator search functionality has been updated with a dropdown of usernames that can be selected.
See image.
A time range filter has been added with custom and preset ranges (Last 24 Hours, Last 7 Days, etc.).
See image.
The manual refresh button now reloads the list without reloading the entire page.
The Export CSV button downloads the filtered audit log.

blocks.text: To learn more, see AI Guard Audit Log.

blocks.item: AI Guard now supports GitHub Copilot Enterprise in Visual Studio (VS) Code.
Webhook calls with Anthropic now display "Anthropic" as the client name in Transaction Details.

blocks.heading: Conversation View for Proxy Mode Transactions

blocks.text: Multi-turn conversations can now be viewed directly in the AI Guard dashboard in Proxy mode. Instead of reviewing individual transactions in isolation, admins can now see the full conversation thread, making it easier to follow the context behind a flagged or logged interaction.
See image.
From the Anthropic console, admins can now test the webhook connection with AI Guard.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Tenant Settings.

blocks.item: Policy Control Name Column for Events: Policy Control Name is a new column added to the dashboard's events view. This gives admins clear visibility into exactly which policy control was matched for a given event, making it faster to trace and investigate policy matches.
Resizable Dashboard Columns: All columns are now resizable on the dashboard.

blocks.text: AI Guard now supports a new log export destination, CrowdStrike SIEM Direct Export, alongside the existing S3-dependent CrowdStrike option. You can now choose between exporting directly to the CrowdStrike HEC endpoint or routing event content through an intermediary AWS S3 bucket, depending on your existing setup.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing AI Guard Log Exports.

blocks.heading: New CrowdStrike Parser for AI Guard

blocks.text: CrowdStrike has updated their portal to include a new parser for AI Guard under the Generic bender connection type as zscaler-aiguard. This allows CrowdStrike users to select the AI Guard-specific parser when configuring a new data connector, rather than relying on the generic template parser.
See image.

blocks.item: Increased Topic Definition Character Limit: The character limit for Topic definitions in policy configuration has been increased from its previous limit to 1000 characters, giving admins more room to write detailed, precise topic definitions when building Topic policies.

Expanded LLM Provider Match Criteria Limit: The LLM Provider field used for match criteria in Policy control now supports up to 100 entries, up from the previous limit of 10. This allows admins to define broader and more granular policies across a wider range of LLM providers without hitting capacity constraints.

Policy Configuration Version Information: Detectors now include version information in the Policy Configuration UI in AI Guard, giving admins and security teams clearer visibility into which version of a detector is in use.
Base64 Support for Detectors: All detectors now support base64.

blocks.text: AI Guard now supports Copilot.com, offering data protection for direct web browser interactions with Copilot. Request and response blocking are both supported, along with custom messages, providing granular control and clear user communication.
To ensure proper connectivity and policy enforcement, the following ZIA configuration URL is required:

blocks.item: www.copilot.com

blocks.text: To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.

AI Guard now supports Copilot in Excel, offering robust data protection for spreadsheet interactions. Request and response blocking are both supported, along with custom messages, providing granular control and clear user communication.
To ensure proper connectivity and policy enforcement, the following ZIA configuration URL is required:

blocks.item: augloop.office.com

blocks.text: To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.

blocks.heading: Event Log Export Tools Field Filter

blocks.text: Log exports can now be configured to filter out the Tools fields from exported event logs. This field is enabled by default for new and existing exports.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing AI Guard Log Exports.

AI Guard can now integrate with Anthropic Claude's inference hooks to inspect and evaluate prompts against a tenant's detection policy in real time. AI Guard responds with an Allow or Deny verdict, which determines whether Claude proceeds to generate a response or the prompt is blocked.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Tenant Settings.

blocks.item: Malicious URL Detection in Prompt Policies: Malicious URLs can now be configured as a detection category within prompt detection policies on the policy configuration page. This expands your ability to identify and control URL-based threats embedded in user prompts.
Pattern Detector Configuration Limit Increased: The Text (Pattern) detector now supports up to 100 regex patterns per policy, increased from the previous limit of 10.
Regex Pattern Length Limit for Text Detector: Individual regex patterns in the Text (Pattern) detector can now be up to 3,000 characters in length, increased from the previous limit.

CSV Export for Dashboard Events: Dashboard event tables now support CSV export in addition to the existing PDF export option. This provides greater flexibility when sharing, analyzing, or archiving flagged interactions.

blocks.text: In the Secrets detector, the US Government ID category has been updated to support only Detect and Disable options.

Policies currently configured with BLOCK or ALLOW for this category will automatically transition to Disabled mode when any Secrets policy configuration updates are applied. All newly created policies will have the US Government ID category set to Disabled by default.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding and Managing AI Guard Policy Configurations.

AI Guard for User's tenancy restriction feature allows you to restrict user traffic access either to personal accounts, enterprise accounts, or both, and apply different access-control rules to each. This feature is currently available for Anthropic and OpenAI.
See image.
To learn more about account-type policy control, see Managing Tenant Settings.
AI Guard now supports streaming responses for Microsoft 365 Copilot, ensuring that real-time AI interactions are inspected and protected as they are generated.
The following Microsoft 365 apps are currently supported by AI Guard:

blocks.item: M365 Web Experience (Web Browser)
M365 Desktop App (Windows and Mac)
Copilot in Word (Desktop App and Web Browser)
Copilot in Outlook (Web Browser)

blocks.text: To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.

The prompt allowlist for AI Guard allows you to track and manage any prompts that you wish to allow that may otherwise be blocked by an existing AI Guard policy. Prompts added to the allowlist are fully encrypted, so the prompt content remains protected end-to-end.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Prompt Allowlist.

When viewing transaction details in the dashboard, the prompt and response fields are grouped into separate rows (Detections / Action / Tags) for clearer, at-a-glance readability. Each detection tag group now expands via the View details link.
See image.

When a prompt contains PII or Secrets, matched spans are highlighted inline in both the original and masked views using action-colored background fills. Hovering a span shows a tooltip with the masked replacement and confidence (e.g. "Masked as: IP_ADDRESS-1 · 73% confidence"), or the original value and confidence in the masked view.
See image.
To learn more, see About Dashboard.

This release overhauls how flagged Prompt-Injection chunks are surfaced in the Transaction Details view. The previous highlighting is replaced with a more clear approach, a sticky confidence legend makes it easy to navigate flagged chunks, and a new Annotate mode that labels each chunk for precise review.

blocks.item: Confidence-Tiered Highlighting: Flagged text chunks are now grouped by confidence tier, so you can quickly gauge how strongly each chunk was flagged.
≥ 90%: Highest-confidence injection chunks.
70–89%: Medium confidence.
50–69%: Lower confidence.
See image.
Sticky Confidence Legend: A sticky "Prompt injection confidence" legend stays in view while scrolling and only renders the tiers that actually have flagged chunks.
Click a tier: Clicking on the prompt injection confidence will scroll to the first prompt chunk in that confidence tier. Clicking again cycles to the next chunk.
See image.
Hovering over a tier: Dims all other text and non-matching tier labels, isolating the relevant chunks for quick visual scanning.
See image.

Annotate Mode: A new Annotate toggle in the legend turns on detailed chunk labeling for side-by-side comparison and reference. Each flagged prompt chunk gets a numbered marker ([1], [2], etc.) at its end and also receives a distinct pastel background color so individual chunks are easy to tell apart.
See image.

blocks.text: To learn more, see About Dashboard.
Windsurf is now available as a supported provider.
To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.

The Dashboard page has been updated to include more granular detection details (Dashboard > Details > Detection Summary), including detected entities and confidence scores. Users can now view comprehensive data for both request and response events, providing deeper insight into trigger conditions.
See image.
To learn more, see About AI Guard Dashboard.

blocks.item: Japanese is now available as an option in the Language detector.
The Secrets detector has been enhanced to allow for disabling any unwanted labels from detections.
Some upcoming PII labels have been added with only Detect or Disabled actions available at this time.
The update on existing policies should be on the PII detector configuration page.
See image.

Existing policies must be manually updated to move the updated labels to Disabled mode. Ensure that both Request and Response policies are updated with any small change (e.g., updating a Severity label) before saving so that the new label updates appear.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Adding and Managing AI Guard Policy Configurations.

blocks.item: Dashboard: Optimized page load times for the event dashboard across all operating modes.

Proxy Changes in User Mode: The Request Blocking message for Claude has been updated in browsers when there is no custom message. The expected message behavior is: "This request has been blocked by your organization."

blocks.text: Mistral Vibe (formerly Le Chat) is now available as a supported provider. To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.

blocks.heading: Gemini CLI Support in Proxy Mode

blocks.text: Google Gemini (command-line interface) CLI support is now available for AI Guard in Proxy mode. To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.
Bedrock Anthropic support for traffic is now available in User mode. To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.

blocks.item: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Misc. enhancements and bug fixes.

blocks.text: AI Guard 2.15.1 introduces enhanced data integration capabilities and significantly expands administrative control through advanced Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). These updates are designed to strengthen governance, flexibility, and operational visibility for enterprise environments. Previously, the only supported roles were Administrator, Editor, and Viewer.
See image.
RBAC management includes:

blocks.item: Support for custom roles and permissions, replacing the previous fixed role model.
Fine-grained access control over administrative functions.
Ability to tailor permissions based on organizational needs and responsibilities.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Managing Role-Based Access Control in AI Guard.

blocks.heading: Azure Data Explorer (ADX) Log Export Support

blocks.text: AI Guard now supports seamless integration with Azure Data Explorer (ADX), enabling efficient export and analysis of event data.
See image.
Key capabilities include:

blocks.item: Streaming event metadata and content directly to ADX via Azure Event Hub.
Enabling advanced analytics, querying, and long-term data storage.
Improve visibility into AI activity, policy enforcement, and system behavior.
Support scalable and high-performance data ingestion pipelines.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Managing AI Guard Log Exports.

Support added for the Codex application. Codex is an OpenAI code agent and doesn't require additional Internet & SaaS (ZIA) configuration for URLs if you've already configured the forwarding for ChatGPT traffic from ZIA. It supports request blocking and response blocking.
GitHub Copilot is now available as a supported provider for prompt visibility and blocking. Response inspection is not yet supported.
To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.
From the Tenant Settings page in AI Guard, you are now able to:

blocks.item: View your AWS Account ID in the General tab. This is used for optional AWS integrations such as log exports to AWS S3 buckets or optional AWS customer-managed keys for encryption.
Start a manual sync with ZIA outside the scheduled batch window in the Integrations tab.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Managing Tenant Settings and Managing AI Guard Log Exports.

blocks.item: Microsoft 365 & Copilot:
M365 Response Blocking: Added support for response blocking cases.
M365 Response Blocking Options Hidden: M365 default suggestions won't appear for a response blocking use case.
Copilot Think Deeper Mode: Added support for consistent responses in Think Deeper Mode.
ChatGPT Message Behavior: Added support to ensure ChatGPT generally follows configured custom or standard block messaging.
UI Enhancement: Changes to a policy that have occurred since its creation are now displayed as an entry on the Audit Log page.

blocks.text: During AI Guard tenant creation, all default LLM providers are now:

blocks.item: Automatically provisioned.
Pre-configured and ready to use.

blocks.text: This eliminates the need for manual setup, reduces operational overhead, and accelerates start-up time. This has no impact on existing customers.
ElevenLabs (text-to-speech mode) is now available as a supported provider.
To learn more, see Integrating ZIA with AI Guard.

blocks.item: Microsoft 365 Response Truncation: Resolved an issue where responses were being truncated unexpectedly on the dashboard page.
Claude API Error with PII Masking: Fixed a bug causing 400 errors when PII masking was enabled in Claude-code usage workflows.
Dashboard Filter Dropdown Issue: Resolved an issue where not all filter options were visible in dashboard dropdown menus.

blocks.text: The IP Detector is a critical new feature designed to safeguard proprietary or sensitive information provided by users as background data (the "context") for language model interactions. It analyzes a user's subsequent input/query against the provided context to determine if the input is semantically similar enough to indicate a potential leak, paraphrase, or direct exposure of the sensitive source material.
This ensures that the original context is protected from being inadvertently or maliciously recycled through the input prompt itself.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding and Managing AI Guard Policy Configurations.
On the Insights page, when users click on a specific bar in a PII graph, a pop-up window will appear with all transactions that contributed to that bar in the chart.
See image.
To learn more, see About AI Guard Insights.

blocks.heading: Support for Disabling Policy Actions in PII Detectors

blocks.text: In addition to the Allow, Block, and Detect options for policy actions, PII detectors have the ability to Disable policy actions. If a label is selected as Disabled, it is not covered under PII detections.
The "Person's name" label is defaulted to Disabled.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding and Managing AI Guard Policy Configurations.

blocks.heading: Filter Log Exports with Prompt Action

blocks.text: Log Exports now allow filtering logs based on prompt actions. The new policy filtering options are Export Allowed/Detected Prompts and Export Blocked Prompts.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing AI Guard Log Exports.

In the Tenant Settings Security tab, you have the option to automatically delete chat history of response blocking cases for providers like ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini.
See image.

blocks.item: Implemented auto ordering of rule execution within policy controls to prevent conflict errors and ensure consistent policy enforcement.
The default detection threshold for PII has been updated to 0.5.
AI Guard now supports dual-mode login, enabling both Authentication Service and email-based authentication.
Logos updated for providers.

blocks.heading: Dashboard and Insights Export PDF Option

blocks.text: Users can export reports directly in PDF format from the Dashboard and Insights pages.
See image.
To learn more, see About AI Guard Dashboard and About AI Guard Insights.

MaxAI (api.maxai.me), Lovable (api.lovable.dev), Bolt (bolt.new), and Google Gemini Code (*.gemini.google.com and cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com) have been added as supported providers in User mode. Only request blocking is supported on these new providers.
